```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, dpi = 150)
has_supercell <- requireNamespace("Seurat", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("SuperCell", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("mcRigor", quietly = TRUE)
has_seacells <- has_supercell && requireNamespace("basilisk", quietly = TRUE)
```

When the starting point is single-cell data, `cellprograms` can aggregate
cells into **metacells** — transcriptomically homogeneous small groups —
before pseudobulk factorization. The default backend is
[SuperCell 2.0](https://github.com/GfellerLab/SuperCell) (pure R, no
Python), selected by a preregistered benchmark against SEACells on
membership fidelity and downstream program recovery; the
[SEACells](https://github.com/dpeerlab/SEACells) backend (isolated, pinned
basilisk Python environment built on first use) remains available. Both
backends are QC'd with mcRigor and stratified so that **metacells never
cross the grouping variables** (donor x cell type by default).

This vignette runs the full workflow on a simulated dataset with planted
cell-type identity, then feeds the metacell counts into
`fit_celltype_programs()`.

## Simulate a small single-cell dataset

Two donors x two cell types, 80 cells each, 200 genes. Each cell type gets a
private marker block; everything else is background Poisson noise.

```{r fixture}
library(cellprograms)
set.seed(11)

n_per <- 80
types <- c("Tcells", "Bcells")
donors <- c("donor1", "donor2")
groups <- rep(paste0(rep(donors, each = length(types)), "_", rep(types, length(donors))),
              each = n_per)

lam <- matrix(0.5, nrow = 200, ncol = length(groups))
markers <- list(Tcells = 1:12, Bcells = 13:24)
for (g in unique(groups)) {
  type <- sub(".*_", "", g)
  cols <- which(groups == g)
  lam[markers[[type]], cols] <- 8
}
counts <- Matrix::Matrix(rpois(200 * length(groups), as.vector(lam)),
                         nrow = 200, ncol = length(groups), sparse = TRUE)
rownames(counts) <- paste0("gene", seq_len(200))
colnames(counts) <- paste0("cell", seq_len(length(groups)))

meta <- data.frame(
  donor = sub("_.*", "", groups),
  celltype = sub(".*_", "", groups),
  row.names = colnames(counts)
)

obj <- Seurat::CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts, meta.data = meta)
obj <- Seurat::NormalizeData(obj, verbose = FALSE)
obj <- Seurat::FindVariableFeatures(obj, nfeatures = 60, verbose = FALSE)
obj <- Seurat::ScaleData(obj, verbose = FALSE)
obj <- Seurat::RunPCA(obj, npcs = 10, verbose = FALSE)
```

## Build metacells per group

`MetacellsByGroupsSuperCell()` runs SuperCell's `SCimplify` separately
within each `group.by` stratum and stores everything under the Seurat
object's `misc` (key `"SuperCell"` by default):

```{r metacells, eval = has_supercell}
obj <- MetacellsByGroupsSuperCell(obj,
                                  group.by = c("donor", "celltype"),
                                  cells_per_metacell = 20,
                                  min_cells = 50,
                                  n_top_genes = 60,
                                  n_pc = 10,
                                  seed = 11, verbose = FALSE)
res <- GetMetacellSuperCell(obj)
names(res)
```

`cells_per_metacell` is SuperCell's `gamma` — the target number of native
cells per metacell. Alternatively pass `target_metacells` (approximate
metacell count per group), which is reached by log-gamma bisection. The
result carries the metacell Seurat object, per-metacell mcRigor QC, fit
statistics, the parameters used, and any skipped groups:

```{r qc, eval = has_supercell}
head(res$qc)                 # mcDiv, dubious flag, ZeroRate per metacell
res$skipped_groups           # groups dropped (e.g. too few cells) - usually empty
```

Groups with too few cells (below `min_cells`) are skipped with a warning
rather than failing the call — check `skipped_groups` when working with
small strata.

### The same workflow with SEACells

`MetacellsByGroupsSEACells()` has the same interface and return structure;
it fits SEACells archetypes per group in the basilisk Python environment
(results under `misc[["SEACells"]]`, with the cells x archetypes soft
assignment matrix in the result):

```{r seacells, eval = has_seacells}
obj_sea <- MetacellsByGroupsSEACells(obj,
                                     group.by = c("donor", "celltype"),
                                     cells_per_metacell = 20,
                                     min_cells = 50,
                                     n_top_genes = 60,
                                     n_pc = 10,
                                     seed = 11, verbose = FALSE)
res_sea <- GetMetacellSEACells(obj_sea)
names(res_sea)
```

## Optimize the number of metacells (gamma)

SuperCell's `gamma` is the number of native cells per metacell — the
granularity. `OptimizeGammaSuperCell()` refits across candidate gammas per
group and picks the winner by the mcRigor optimization score:

```{r optimize, eval = has_supercell}
opt <- OptimizeGammaSuperCell(obj,
                              group.by = "donor",
                              gammas = c(10, 20),
                              n_top_genes = 60,
                              n_pc = 10,
                              min_cells = 50,
                              mcrigor_args = list(Nrep = 5),
                              seed = 11, verbose = FALSE)
opt$optimal_gamma            # winning gamma per donor group
opt$scores                   # mcRigor score per gamma x group
```

Gammas whose membership collapses to a single metacell are dropped with a
warning and excluded from the pick rather than crashing the run. The
SEACells equivalent is `OptimizeGammaSEACells()` (same arguments; there
`gamma` counts archetypes instead of native cells per metacell).

## Metacell counts feed the program fit directly

```{r programs, eval = has_supercell}
mc <- res$metacell_object
counts_mc <- SeuratObject::LayerData(mc[["RNA"]], layer = "counts")  # genes x metacells
by_type <- split(colnames(mc), mc$celltype)
pb <- lapply(by_type, function(cells) t(as.matrix(counts_mc[, cells, drop = FALSE])))

x <- as_cell_program_data(pb)
fit <- fit_celltype_programs(x, loading_prior = "point_laplace",
                             max_factors = 4, features = "variable",
                             n_variable_genes = 100)
fit <- canonicalize_programs(fit)
program_summary(fit)[, c("cell_type", "n_programs", "R2", "elbo")]
```

The planted structure survives the aggregation: each cell type's programs
are dominated by its private marker block.

```{r markers, eval = has_supercell, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
marker_expr <- as.matrix(counts_mc[unlist(markers), , drop = FALSE])
marker_expr <- t(scale(t(marker_expr)))
df <- data.frame(
  metacell = factor(colnames(marker_expr), levels = colnames(marker_expr)),
  gene = rep(rownames(marker_expr), times = ncol(marker_expr)),
  z = as.vector(marker_expr)
)
ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(metacell, gene, fill = z)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile() +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "metacell", y = "marker gene") +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                 axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 6))
```
